title: Some feedback
body:
Dear Microsoft To Do team,
 
First of all, I would like to express my appreciation for the user-friendly interface and functionality of Microsoft To Do. It has been an invaluable tool for managing my daily tasks.
 
However, I would like to suggest an improvement regarding the recurring tasks feature. Currently, when I complete a recurring task late, the missed instances continue to appear with future dates, causing a backlog of tasks that can become confusing and clutter the overview.
 
I would like to propose an option for users to automatically delete all missed instances when a recurring task is completed late, and allow the recurrence to continue from the most recent date. This would greatly help in keeping the task list organized and prevent duplicates or outdated tasks from appearing.
 
This feature would significantly improve the workflow, especially for users like myself who frequently rely on high-frequency recurring tasks.
 
Thank you in advance for considering my suggestion. I look forward to future updates and improvements to Microsoft To Do.
 
Best regards,

- When a notification of a task pops up on my Home Screen, I tap the reminder/notification and mark the task as completed when I have done so. But very often, I visit the app some later and the completed task (from the notification) is still in the list, unmarked. This makes the marking of a notification very useless. And more important: when it's a recurring task, there will be no notification/reminder the next time cause in the list it was still unmarked.

Sinds we verplicht moesten overstappen op Todo werkt de synchronisatie van lijstjes erg slecht. Als we op 1 iPhone een item toevoegen, wordt hij soms wel en soms niet getoond op een andere iPhone. Ook werkt synchronisatie inconsequent op de browser.

Het product is voor ons onbruikbaar geworden. We hebben contact gezocht met support en die zeggen alleen: “het probleem is bekend, we gaan het fixen”. title: Basic alternative to OmniFocus if moving from Mac to Windows
body: If, unfortunately, you need to move from Mac to Windows - but you still use an iPhone - you’ll likely need to find a replacement for OmniFocus that syncs across all your devices. The Omni people for some reason refuse to make a Windows app, and a web-based version was promised but is not yet here. Microsoft’s ToDo can be an option. Functionality is very basic and some choices are puzzling, like the large estate of the screen wasted for useless illustrations and huge titles. But it’s free, so what can’t really complain.
